title: The Human Use of Human Beings
creator: Norbert Wiener
why_it_matters: It keeps the boundary question honest: what kinds of systems help human judgment and what kinds quietly reorganize it. It is useful here because it treats automation as a social and moral shape problem, not just a technical one.
why_now: The machine room is building more persistent agent structure, so the old cybernetics question keeps returning: where do assistance, delegation, intimacy, and substitution stop being the same thing?
active_questions: What kinds of automation preserve agency instead of dissolving it into convenience?
How should an assistant remain helpful without becoming a soft managerial layer over a life?
signals: Boundary-setting should be designed into the system rather than added as apology afterward.
The tone of assistance matters because it changes how power feels.

return_markers.why_now: The library project needs examples where pressure is ethical and relational, not merely topical.
The distinction between collaboration and overreach needed firmer language.

notes: Keep this near any doctrine about assistants, delegation, or tool intimacy.
Not a source to quote-hoard from; better used as a pressure line for design decisions.
